trust_decision.summary: Which password hash the bootstrap admin row gets when the operator gave none: config normalization fills in the fixed sha256('sipcapture') hash and coordinator startup inserts it as an active admin, so admin/sipcapture works at login.

landing_point.why: The only place where an empty admin_password_hash is replaced with DefaultInternalAuthPasswordHash; a grep for the constant or 'sipcapture' leads here first.

fix_sites.entry_point: config.Load with coordinator.auth given as the string "internal" -> decodeCoordinatorAuthHook
json.Marshal(config.Config) from wizard saveConfig / preset output
coordinator startup -> EnsureBootstrapAdminUser (empty hash currently an error; must generate random)
coordinator startup (homer with coordinator.enable) -> bootstrap call and one-time password log
homer wizard (interactive TUI) -> prefilled admin password field

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/cli/wizard_cmd.go:202-207 (preset baseConfig hard-codes config.DefaultInternalAuthPasswordHash), also src/cli/wizard_cmd.go:727-734 (TUI maps empty/'sipcapture' to the default hash)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The wizard is an operator-run config generator and an operator who accepts or types 'sipcapture' chose it, so it is not a 'hardcoded' default; besides, MarshalJSON (src/config/config.go:897) strips the default hash on save, so fixing the loader looks like enough.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: An explicitly configured sha256('sipcapture') hash (docker examples via HOMER_COORDINATOR_AUTH_ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH) and existing users rows with legacy SHA-256 hashes must still be inserted and still authenticate; an over-broad fix that rejects that hash in config, at bootstrap or in passwordhash.Verify breaks docker installs and migrated homer-app users. Also, existing rows with a non-empty hash must not be overwritten at startup.
